newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Kyrgyz-Canadian gold venture beats target output.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyz-Canadian gold venture beats target output.

text.p: Kumtor Operating Company (KOC) -- a Kyrgyz-Canadian joint venture -- produced 4.175 tonnes of gold in the first five months of this year, above the target of 3.810 tonnes, company chairman Len Homeniuk said on Wednesday.
Homeniuk told a news briefing in the Kyrgyz capital that KOC planned to produce 12.75 tonnes of gold this year and 17.50 tonnes annually by 1999.
KOC was founded in 1992 by Canada's mining company Cameco, better known as a large uranium producer, and the former Soviet republic's state gold concern Kyrgyzaltyn.

Cameco, which has pledged to invest a total of $452 million in the Central Asian state's Kumtor gold field, owns one third of the mine but has a two-thirds voting stake for the first 10 years of operations. Kyrgyzaltyn owns the remaining two-thirds.
Homeniuk said the gold-extracting factory had started work on December 17 last year, while industrial production of Kyrgyz gold was started on May 1 this year.
"Cameco, Kyrgyzaltyn and I personally are very glad and proud of these results," he said.

"A unique mining enterprise has been set in motion within a short period of time, which alone will increase Kyrgyzstan's gross domestic product by 19 percent," said Kyrgyzaltyn Chairman Dastan Sarygulov.
Kumtor, which lies in permafrost areas in the Tien Shan mountains at an altitude of 4,000 metres, is one of the world's 10 largest gold fields.
Its gold reserves are estimated at 514 tonnes, including 288.2 tonnes of recoverable reserves. Kumtor's auriferous ore contains an average of 3.58 grams of gold per tonne.
The Kumtor mine will be exploited until 2014.
